passage:
Subject: okay so there's this girl
Hemant,
Don't laugh. There's a girl in my Economics section, Tanushree. On the first day, when Prof. Bose's mic died, she stood up and did his voice so perfectly the whole class cracked up, and even he laughed. She talks in class like she has never once worried about being wrong.
We've spoken maybe four times. Once about the canteen samosas, once about a quiz, twice in the library queue. That's it.
And yet. I've already imagined us at the college fest, then road-tripping to Goa after finals, then her meeting Amma, who would definitely love her. I've decided her favourite colour is green because of her bag.
Okay, typing it out, I can see I've built a whole person from four chats. But I swear she's brilliant.
Reply soon and tell me I'm not mad.
Raghav

qa.q: How many times has Raghav spoken to Tanushree?
qa.a: They've spoken maybe four times.

qa.q: What does Raghav's imagined road trip and Amma meeting suggest about his feelings?
qa.a: Raghav is dazzled and excited, imagining a whole future with Tanushree from four short chats.

qa.q: What could Raghav do to see the real Tanushree rather than the imagined one?
qa.a: Raghav could spend more ordinary time talking with her, in class or in a group, and let her show who she is before planning any future.

qa.q: How might Tanushree see these same four conversations?
qa.a: Tanushree may see them as friendly chats with a classmate, with no idea Raghav has already pictured road trips and family meetings.

grounding: Shows a student drawn to a classmate's humour and confidence who imagines a future from a few conversations, filling in the blanks.

Neelam, stop smiling, I'm serious. You know Mihir from design studio? The one who presented the bus-stop project and made the jury laugh three times? He walks up to the pin-up wall like it's his own living room. I've never been that sure of anything in my life.
We talked after studio on Monday for about ten minutes. About fonts! And he said my sketches "have a pulse", and I've been replaying it since.
I've decided he probably reads a lot. And he's definitely kind to his mother. And he'd be the kind of person who remembers your chai order.
What? Okay, I don't actually know any of that. I know he's funny, I know he's confident and I know he likes fonts. The rest I might have, um, invented. 😅
But it's a nice invention, na? Gargi is allowed one nice invention.

qa.q: What did Mihir say about Gargi's sketches?
qa.a: Mihir said Gargi's sketches 'have a pulse'.

qa.q: How does Gargi feel about Mihir, and what shows it?
qa.a: Gargi is thrilled and a bit starstruck by Mihir's humour and confidence, replaying one compliment since Monday and imagining what kind of person he is.

qa.q: What could Gargi keep in mind at this early stage?
qa.a: Gargi could enjoy the crush while remembering most of the picture is guesswork, and get to know Mihir through real conversations before deciding who he is. 🙂

qa.q: What would change if Neelam simply agreed with everything Gargi imagined?
qa.a: Gargi might build even more on guesses; Neelam's smile helps Gargi notice the gap between facts and wishes.

grounding: Illustrates a student's infatuation with a classmate's humour and confidence, with the imagined person filling gaps that a few conversations left.

Dear Anu,

You asked about hostel life. Forget hostel life. There is a boy in my economics tutorial called Hemant, and I think I might be in trouble.

He is the funniest person I've ever met. Yesterday the professor's microphone died and Hemant did the rest of the lecture in a perfect radio-announcer voice until even the professor laughed. He walks into class like he owns it.

We've talked exactly three times. Once about the canteen samosas, once about a film, once about nothing. And I already know what our flat would look like. Books everywhere. A cat. He would make me laugh every morning.

I know. I KNOW. I don't even know his surname. But you should see how he smiles when he's about to say something ridiculous.

Don't tell Amma.

Your didi,
Kavitha

qa.q: How many times has Kavitha talked with Hemant?
qa.a: Exactly three times.

qa.q: How does Kavitha feel about Hemant, and what does the imagined flat show?
qa.a: She feels excited and infatuated; imagining their flat after three talks shows she is filling in the blanks with a future she wishes for.

qa.q: What would you advise Kavitha at this stage?
qa.a: Enjoy the crush, but get to know Hemant slowly beyond his jokes, so she learns who he really is rather than who she imagines.

qa.q: How might Hemant see those three conversations?
qa.a: To him they may have been just friendly, pleasant chats, and he may have no idea she is already imagining a shared flat.

grounding: Kavitha is drawn to Hemant's humour and confidence and imagines a whole future from three conversations, showing infatuation filling in the blanks.

passage:
So you want the embarrassing story? Fine. I'm Raghav, second year, and last month I was completely gone over a girl called Gurleen.

She was in my debate society. She stood up on the first day and destroyed the opposing team with one joke, and everyone was laughing, even them. I thought, that's it, that's the one.

We spoke maybe four times after practice. She liked old Hindi songs. That was enough. In my head we were already travelling to Spiti together, she was meeting my parents, we had inside jokes.

Then one evening I heard her talk about wanting to move abroad after college and never come back, and I felt this jolt. Because I'd never asked. I'd just decided who she was. The Gurleen in my head was mostly me, with her face on.

qa.q: What did Gurleen like, according to Raghav?
qa.a: Old Hindi songs.

qa.q: Why does Raghav feel a jolt when he hears Gurleen's plans?
qa.a: He feels surprised and a little foolish, realising he had imagined who she was without ever asking.

qa.q: What could Raghav do differently now?
qa.a: He could get to know Gurleen through real conversations, asking about her plans and values, instead of imagining them.

qa.q: What would change if Gurleen knew about the imagined trip to Spiti?
qa.a: She might feel flattered but also uneasy, since she barely knows Raghav and he had pictured a future for her.

grounding: Raghav is drawn to Gurleen's humour and confidence and imagines a future from a few chats, until he realises the person he saw was partly wished for.

Monday. Jahnavi noticed him at the college fest, the boy on stage doing stand-up about hostel food. Everyone laughed. So did she, too loudly. His name, her friend Preeti said, was Shaan.

Thursday, three days later. They talked for twenty minutes near the library about a comedy show. He was even funnier up close. That night Jahnavi lay awake imagining them at the same fest next year, him dedicating a joke to her from the stage. She told Preeti, "He's so sure of himself. I love that."

Sunday, the next week. At a group lunch, Shaan made fun of the waiter's accent. Everyone laughed except Jahnavi. She looked at him for a long moment.

"Still in love?" Preeti whispered.

"I don't know," Jahnavi said. "I think I made most of him up."

qa.q: What was Shaan doing on stage at the college fest?
qa.a: Stand-up about hostel food.

qa.q: What does Jahnavi's long look at Shaan at lunch suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she is surprised and disappointed, seeing a side of him that didn't match the person she had imagined.

qa.q: What could help Jahnavi at this stage?
qa.a: She could keep getting to know Shaan slowly and notice how he treats others, not just how funny he is on stage.

qa.q: How does Preeti see Jahnavi's crush?
qa.a: Preeti seems amused and a bit teasing, watching her friend move from starstruck to doubtful.

grounding: Over a week Jahnavi falls for Shaan's humour and confidence and imagines a future, then sees she had filled in the blanks with a wished-for person.

passage: Keerthana, sit with me a minute. Your Paati was nineteen once, you know. In the hostel they called me Nimmi, because Nirmala was too long to shout down a corridor. There was a boy in our chemistry batch, Mohan, who could make the whole lab laugh when a burette leaked, and who answered the professor without a single stammer. We spoke perhaps four times, near the cycle stand, about nothing much. By the fourth time I had already planned our house by the river and decided he loved old film songs the way I did. He never once mentioned songs, kutty. I painted the empty spaces with my own colours. At night I wrote his name in the margins of my notes and felt dizzy with it. Only much later did I wonder who he really was, under all my paint.

qa.q: Where did Nirmala and Mohan talk?
qa.a: They spoke perhaps four times, near the cycle stand, about nothing much.

qa.q: What was Nirmala feeling as she planned a house by the river after only four talks?
qa.a: She felt giddy and excited, so thrilled by Mohan's humour and confidence that she filled every unknown with her own hopes, like his love of film songs.

qa.q: At this stage, what could the young Nirmala have done before building a whole future around Mohan?
qa.a: She could have enjoyed the attraction while getting to know him slowly, asking what he actually liked instead of deciding he loved her film songs.

qa.q: How might Mohan have seen those few talks by the cycle stand?
qa.a: To Mohan they were probably light, friendly chats with a batchmate; he likely had no idea she had already imagined a house by the river.

grounding: Shows a student drawn to a classmate's humour and confidence who imagines a whole future, and his tastes, from only a few conversations.
